text:
alex: quick note — onboarding report: js-sdk@2.4.x sample breaks in local Cloudflare + Vite dev. Browser console: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' and network shows two /v1/token POSTs.
mira: can you paste the package.json exports + the import line?
alex: exports snapshot in the package: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
alex: sample just does `import { Redwood } from 'redwood-js-sdk'`.
sam: this is the bundler/export map interplay we've warned about. Some dev servers will resolve the import condition but still wrap modules for HMR which can inject CJS shims around .mjs. If an .mjs ends up inside a CJS wrapper you get that runtime syntax error.
oliver: double token POSTs likely mean two instances of the SDK ended up in the bundle (esm + cjs) or init ran twice because HMR re-evaluated. We should make init idempotent.
mira: short-term workaround for samples: import the explicit ESM edge entry `import { Redwood } from 'redwood-js-sdk/dist/esm/edge.mjs'` and add a README note for Vite+Wrangler dev.
alex: confirmed workaround fixes the syntax error and removes duplicate auth requests. Not a long-term UX win though.
sam: suggested fixes: 1) add module-scoped init guard to debounce token fetches, 2) add a small edge-specific entry file (dist/esm/edge.mjs) and document it, 3) add CI smoke test that runs edge sample with wrangler dev to catch regressions.
oliver: also check typings: TS sometimes picks up cjs d.ts and editors show wrong signatures. We should ensure our package.json points to correct types for ESM consumers or consider conditional types mapping.
mira: open RDW issue and tag infra + docs. @ops-bot can you create one?
ops-bot: Created RDW-5512 — "Export-map + bundler HMR causes edge import errors and duplicate SDK init" (labels: devex, sdk-exports, edge)

alex: I'll update the edge sample README with the explicit import workaround and mention recommended bundler flags.
sam: I'll prototype a tiny init guard that sets a module-scoped promise and prevents concurrent token fetches. If two copies load we also log their resolved filenames to help debugging.
oliver: avoid adding nonstandard export conditions like "edge" in package.json; prefer shipping the edge entry file and explicit docs.
mira: once the guard is validated, we should ship a patch (v2.4.1) and add the CI smoke test. If many customers still hit it we can revisit exports revert.
alex: PR for README and sample notes incoming. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
